import html # Pre‑defined HTML template for the invitation. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title}

{event_title}

Date: {event_date}

{event_description}
{additional_notes} """ def build_event_invitation( title_of_event: str, details_of_event: str, when_event_is: str, extra_event_info: str ) -> str: """ Create a secure HTML invitation string. Parameters ---------- title_of_event : str The event's heading or name. details_of_event : str Full description of the event. May contain line breaks or formatting. when_event_is : str Date/time string for the event. extra_event_info : str Any user‑supplied additional notes or instructions. Returns ------- str A sanitized HTML string ready for rendering. """ # Escape all user‑supplied content to prevent XSS (CWE-79). safe_title = html.escape(title_of_event, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(details_of_event, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") safe_date = html.escape(when_event_is, quote=True) # For extra notes we might want to allow simple formatting (e.g., line breaks), # but still escape any HTML. safe_notes = html.escape(extra_event_info, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") # Only include the notes block if there's content. additional_notes_block = f"

Additional Notes: {safe_notes}

" if safe_notes.strip() else "" # Format the invitation with sanitized content. invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_date=safe_date, event_description=safe_description, additional_notes=additional_notes_block ) return invitation_html.strip()
